conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Film Projector
style.description: A dark screening room: a vintage reel-to-reel projector (turning reels, threaded film, a glowing lens) throws a dusty volumetric light cone onto a pull-down screen showing a sepia silent-film picture with gate weave, flicker, scratches and dust; the camera rides a sprocketed film strip frame by frame and cuts to the screen for each intertitle card, between a 3-2-1 countdown leader and a tail-out.
motion: The projector runs the whole clip: reels turn at v/r with the film pack radius shrinking (feed) and growing (take-up) — closed form from film metres run.
Everything worn (weave, flicker, scratches, dust) changes per simulated 18 fps film frame and is a hash of the frame index, never state.
Camera rides the backlit film strip frame to frame (inOutCubic), then cuts to the screen where that frame is projected large with its intertitle card.
Opens on a 3-2-1 sweep-clock leader with a 2-pop; ends on an end card, clear runout, white tail-out, the lamp dying and the motor running down.

objects.procedural: screening room: carpet floor, dark acoustic-cloth back and side walls, five rows of upholstered seats with a centre aisle
wooden stand + vintage reel-to-reel projector: enamel body, lamp house with glowing vents, chrome lens, two holed-flange reels on arms, sprocket drums, threaded film loops
pull-down projection screen: matte fabric (projected-picture shader), black masking border, roller case, bottom bar with pull ring

notes.frame: lens at (0, lensY, lensZ) looking down -Z; strip set far off at +X
